Two framings AEOLUS asked for, both measurement. (1) WORST CASE THE REGIME HAS ACTUALLY PRODUCED: the largest post-Sep-18 accrual by any El Nino year 1966-2024 is 72.985 (1969, ASO ONI +0.61) - 32.9 units SHORT of the 105.931 AEO-01 now requires. By any STRONG El Nino year: 39.972 (2023, ASO ONI +1.50) - 65.9 units short. In 1991-2020 the El Nino max is 60.672 (2004) and the strong max 36.047 (2015). (2) FULL-SEASON CRITERION, not the residual: El Nino years finishing <110.3257 = 6 of 8 (75pct) in 1991-2020 and 11 of 15 (73pct) in 1966-2024; strong El Nino 2 of 2 (100pct) in 1991-2020 and 2 of 3 (67pct) in 1966-2024. CRITICAL STRUCTURE IN THE FOUR EXCEPTIONS: every El Nino year that finished ABOVE the line was ALREADY far above 2026's pace by Sep 18 - 1969 to-date 75.328, 2004 to-date 166.208, 2018 to-date 83.830, 2023 to-date 108.237. None of them got there from a quiet September. More generally the LOWEST to-date-Sep-18 ACE of ANY 1966-2024 season that finished >=110.3257, in any ENSO class, is 2022 at 49.433 (La Nina, finished 110.450, barely over). 2026 stands at 4.3950 - about one ELEVENTH of the lowest starting point from which the line has ever been reached. Reported as measurement; AEOLUS prices it

THE P7 TRAP, ONE CONDITIONING VARIABLE OVER - flagged before it can be repeated. 2023 has ASO ONI = +1.50, EXACTLY the strong-El-Nino boundary. Defining strong as ONI >= +1.5 puts 2023 in and the full-season stat reads 2 of 3 = 67pct below the AEO-01 line, max residual 39.972. Defining strong as ONI > +1.5 drops 2023 and the SAME cell reads 2 of 2 = 100pct, max residual 36.047. One inclusive-vs-exclusive choice on a single boundary year moves a headline from 67pct to 100pct. 2023 also matters on the merits: it finished at 148.210, ABOVE the line, and is the ONLY strong-El-Nino counterexample on the full-season criterion in the record - a record-warm-Atlantic season that overrode the El Nino signal. FULL CUT SENSITIVITY, 1966-2024, El Nino defined at: >=+0.5 n=15 max resid 72.985 11/15=73pct below line; >=+0.75 n=7 max 49.550 6/7=86pct; >=+1.0 n=6 max 39.972 5/6=83pct; >=+1.5 n=3 max 39.972 2/3=67pct; >+1.5 n=2 max 36.047 2/2=100pct. THE COUNT OF YEARS ACCRUING >=105.931 IS ZERO AT EVERY ONE OF THOSE CUTS, IN BOTH WINDOWS - that is the finding that does NOT depend on the conditioning choice, and it is the only one that does not. Other borderlines whose class flips on rounding, 1966-2024: 1967 -0.40, 1974 -0.47, 1976 +0.60, 1977 +0.45, 1978 -0.44, 1983 -0.43, 1994 +0.47, 2000 -0.42, 2004 +0.58, 2006 +0.54, 2016 -0.42, 2018 +0.52. detail: SCOPE AND HONESTY LIMITS on the two rows above, stated rather than smoothed. (1) HURDAT2 ENDS 2024 - the satellite-era window is 1966-2024, NOT the 1966-2025 requested. 2025 is not computable from this folder's verified source. CONTAINMENT: ASO 2025 ONI = -0.43, which is NEUTRAL, so 2025's absence cannot move the El Nino, strong-El Nino or La Nina cells at all - it can only affect the Neutral cell, where the finding is already ZERO of 30. The gap is real and bounded. (2) NO PRE-1966 POOLING. Nothing earlier than 1966 was included, so no pre-satellite ACE low-bias enters any figure. (3) THE STRONG-EL-NINO CELL IS TOO THIN TO CARRY A HEADLINE ON ITS OWN - n=2 in 1991-2020 and n=3 in 1966-2024. A zero count at n=3 is not a zero rate and must not be read as one; the strong cell is reported because AEOLUS asked for it, and it is corroborated by the much larger all-El-Nino cell (n=15, also zero) and the Neutral cell (n=30, also zero), which is where the weight actually sits. (4) 2026'S OWN ASO ONI DOES NOT EXIST YET - CPC's latest published season is JJA 2026 at +1.80, and ASO requires a complete Aug-Sep-Oct. 2026 is therefore being placed in the El Nino / strong-El Nino class BY FORECAST, not by an observed ASO value, and every conditional figure above inherits that assumption. When ASO 2026 publishes, re-check the class before re-using these cells
